reviews.review: This is a game that deserves to attain the status of a cult hit, and I hope it can get there. It's rough around the edges, but the game gets so much [i]right[/i] about the soulslike genre where other games miss the mark. If Dark Souls is a band, then this game is the side-project of the bass player and drummer, and you're seeing them put on one hell of a drunken show in somebody's basement.

This game is a triumph that transcends the genre of "souls-like."

I am a souls veteran having played all 5 games through to completion several times each. I have done speedruns of Bloodborne and DS3 and consider myself a pretty significant fan of the series. Immortal Unchained is not Dark Souls with guns. It is not a souls-like. Although Immortal Unchained has adopted the tangible portions of Dark Souls mechanics(Bonfires, stam bar, estus flask, varied weapons and builds) that are great for Action RPG games in general, its what Toadman has done BEYOND those simple aspects which makes IU so great. 

Set in a living world full of complexities, excellent level design and heart, youll discover that IU doesnt try and blatantly copy souls games in order to capture your interest. Instead, IU captures the intangibles, those feelings you get of discovery and surprise when you locate a new short cut or a different approach to defeating an enemy. Immortal Unchained provoked in me the sense of wonder and awe in the world I was traversing in order to achieve a goal for an entity who I do not yet completely trust. Youll discover NPCs with deep background stories and be granted the opportunity to offer them redemption, or doom them by how you play it all out. In the end, if you want to use souls games as a yardstick, you should value a game by what it does better than the souls series, and IU is filled with qualities that surpass the souls games in implementation and design. 

What Toadman has done is create a game which stands on its own, regardless of whether its "souls-like," with nuanced combat that you learn from, enemies who test you, and who you will learn to punish. You will traverse interconnected worlds that double back and fold upon each other, advance deeper and deeper into planets which are the setting for your adventures as the Immortal. 

Everyone is sleeping on this game. Some reviewers say the game lacks polish, well thats because its a AA. For me, I havent noticed any errors or crashes. Another game from a small dev was poorly reviewed on Metacritic - Demons Souls. If you spend some time playing this game, youll realize the amount of effort and care that went into this game and you can decide for yourself whether youd want to play an upcoming developer's original game and be there on the ground floor.

Can't recommend the game in it's current state. As with many Souls-Like games, it doesn't appear to really understand what makes the Souls game so compelling: challenging, but ultimately fair gameplay. In Souls games, you can always be powerful enough to competently deal with whatever the game throws at you. I'm not saying I'm amazing at those games, but I've done all sort of challenge runs from no rings runs, naked no armor runs, to the infamous SL1 (Level 1) playthroughs on all of them. All of this exemplifies what I said about Souls games: difficult, but fair. Learn and master the mechanics, and you can excel.

So, I'm not going to go into great detail as most of my issue everyone else is saying here, so I'll just make a bullet point list to confirm the issues and you can make your own judgements.

- Gunplay feels flat and weak (plus obnoxious recoil considering that), meele weapons aren't very powerful either, with the bonus that the animations can be long and leave you open to attack
- The number of mobs themselves is super high, and they tend to perfectly completent each others weaknesses, such as crossfires of machinegunners on high ground, with meele enemies low and down the middle. A cool idea, if you could properly exploit and isolate...
- But the level design is such that you can't really do that, so you either have to waste tons of ammo (which is somewhat scarce, and majority of guns are highly inaccurate at range + heavy damage falloff), or your healing items, or both. Either way it's a chore and a bore.
- Checkpoints are spread out, hard to find, and buried behind loads of enemies
- Getting knocked down happens often and is essentially a death sentence, as unlike Souls-Borne games, you take damage when knocked down, and I-Frames on your dodge roll are...inconsistent, at best.
- FPS drops

Overall, a highly frustrating experience. Needs some major rebalancing, most guns need either a significant damage buff or better accuracy to even put you on par with the mobs. Enemy AI is smart, which is cool, but there are far too many of them in a single point of conflict to make clearing the area feel like fun and skillful rather than annoying. I love the idea of "Gun Souls" game, but this game needs a lot of work to meet that potential.

Bought the game on PS4 at release week and a couple of months later on steam. Have been playing it pretty regularly since release. Suffice to say that the game has immense replay value, for exploring the various worlds and doing assorted challenge runs.

The game world and level design impressed me from the start. Levels are superbly interconnected in a variety of ways, including dark souls -type shortcuts you can open and portal gateways that you can open sometimes long after initially finding them since they need keys and protocols you collect while traversing the world. Levels are designed so that there are many places where you, once you've familiarised yourself with the place, can bypass large sections of the map by rolling or "jumping" (there's no actual jump in the game but you can run off a ledge to sort of jump forward) to a lower level / platform and continuing on from there. In terms of level design it's very, very well done.

Combat I've felt is good enough, it could be better (or more varied) but it's quite smooth. Controls are excellent, I don't honestly understand the people who have critiqued them. This plays much better than, say, lords of the fallen or dark souls 2. 

Stat system works well now that weapon requirements and drop/loot locations were overhauled (this was in November), but it probably takes some time and thinking for people to figure it out. It's not instantly intuitive what stats you should raise and which are unimportant for the various weapons. You also get one re-spec item per playthrough. 

NG+ -mode, that was added as a free dlc is also really well done. Different enemy spawn locations (but within "lore realism") on NG+ and the enemy difficulty is maxed out at NG++++.

Immortal: Unchained is the most positive gaming-related surprise of 2018 for me, quite easily. Would recommend.

I paid for I:U on Humble for small price and I expected the key will be gone after. And I did not posted negative reviews for this. What devs did after Humble took keys away? They give another key for the game and for the DLC just for free!

I definitely had a rough start with this game. It felt a little off, and I kind of ran into a brick wall of difficulty early on in the second major world. But then... I dunno. Something just clicked for me, and now the more I play this game, the more I love it.

It's definitely not a game that's for everyone, but if you think the idea sounds cool and you're masochistic enough to make yourself play it until it clicks I cannot possibly recommend this game enough. It's great.

Good game with potential.

Devs were good enough to provide me a new key after the Humble Store pricing error!.

This game is a very under rated souls like gem! this game is a souls like game but the focus is on combat with guns rather than melee weapons. that is to say close range combat is not out of the question, you can make a close range build stacking strength and using shotguns and luanchers and heavy hitting melee weapons, I choose to focus on rifles. the games only flaw is that there are 3 ability scores that boost damage and almost no weapons needs them. the stat system is a little bit flawed but otherwise as someone who has all the dark souls games and loves them I enjoyed this game alot!

Demon's Souls with guns is what I'd call it.

Why not "Dark Souls with guns"?

Well it's lacking in polish while still maintaining a formula that could be passed down to a superior successor without much subtractive design choices.

It's not even necessarily a bad thing that the game lacks polish, it gives it a lot of charm and blunt crudeness to how you combat your enemies. You have a lot more options than you will likely ever use and that's something that is rare in games these days where your tools are limited and you have few choices.

You can make the game more difficult for yourself by choice! Everything you do when it comes to your additional stats per level allocation to the route you decide to take through the game are absolutely free for you to choose as soon as you complete the first boss.

You'll explore 5 brutal and unforgiving zones made up of 20+ different environment designs ranging from the platform of creation itself to a blood forest, a thunderstorm posessed metropolis, caves, sewers, volcanoes, and so on.

Try to beat it without dying. :3

The game is brutal. It starts off slow and basic. The first few bosses aren't varied or cool. The low level guns won't feel badass.

But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if the game doesn't become a different beast when you get passed that start. The maps are giant, and there are a ton of them, and they are interconnected. The level design is clever but deadly. The guns become engines of destruction. Your character slowly stops being a statistic and starts being a hunter as you level up and gain upgrades. There are over a dozen optional bosses, and some of them make Dark Souls look like a joke. The game rewards exploration and strategy. The story has a few wild turns and is told through item descriptions. The game features a new game+ mode with escalating difficulty.

Only negatives I can name are the beginning of the game and the difficulty curve (which will scare most people away).

reviews.review:
I love this game. The screenshots and footage alone piqued my interest because the design is so striking - I really like the neon lights, dark fantasy design mixed with crazy sci-fi elements. It's very distinct, the game oozes a lot of personality and is a labor of love in its design.

Gameplay is really good. Shooting mechanics feel punchy and satisfying, and it's very fast paced. Invulnerability frames are very generous with dodges, so it's not ultra precise about timing which is actually pretty nice, and given some of the enemy types, a wise decision.

Level design is excellent. Very long, winding pathways with interesting environments and variety, chock full of secrets and traps. Really enjoyed going through almost every world. Lots of "wow" moments with epic vistas and colours. Reminded me a lot of the first time I played Dark Souls - completely unaware of what was coming up next and enjoying the surprise of it.

Story is told in a Souls style, indirectly and through tidbits of information. You piece it together and fill in the holes. The lore is really good - pretty grim stuff that reminded me a bit of a mix of WH40k and Dark Souls. The ending too - REALLY liked how it ended. Thought it was an interesting take on an ending which gave me a big grin.

In terms of cons, I'll list them.

-Some enemy designs are very unenjoyable to fight against. The teleporting enemies aren't actually that bad and are very timing based, but the guys with the shields from Apexion are outright annoying. Really don't enjoy fighting them and it feels like a chore.

-Apexion has far too high of a spike in damage at its point in the game. The snipers are extremely powerful and the shielders compound the issue more. This combination didn't work very well and made for a pretty irritating level. Design wise fantastic, but damage output there needs rebalancing. It's very jarring.

-There are a few areas where it's slightly too long of a slog to get through before fighting bosses. Mainly near the end of the game. The mix of enemies in those areas too are very nasty.

-Being stunlocked to death because of a single hit sucks. The teleporting shotgun guys mixed with melee enemies is pretty rubbish. Some of these enemy combinations and the way they attack you is the problem, not necessarily the enemies themselves. Being locked down for so long too, that's a problem.

---

Overall though, I actually think this game is far better than the Mixed rating suggests. I think much of the earlier reviews from launch hamper it, probably because of launch issues and from what I heard some weapon imbalances. Now though, it's well worth grabbing. Apart from a few blemishes, I seriously enjoyed the hell out of this game. As far as I know this is Toadman's first release. For a first release, this is top tier stuff, and I'm really looking forward to seeing more of this universe or other games in the same vein.

Awesome game. Well worth it.
Ultra-hardcore? More like ultra-dumb. I'm sorry, but this game is a mess. Level design is horrible, enemies are boring and controls are wanky. Also, dodge interrupts your reloading. Is this a joke?
